task: I ___ afraid of snakes.
explanation: We use ‘am’ with I.

task: Sam ___ at home last night.
explanation: We use ‘wasn’t’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Isn’t’ - used for the present. ‘Didn’t’ is not used without a verb.

task: I ____ for a bank.
explanation: I/we/you/they — work. He/she/it — works. ‘I’m working’ is the Present Continuous which is incorrect here. The speaker talks in general.

task: I ____ (to watch) that movie yesterday.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. Regular verb + -ed = watch + -ed = watched.

task: He ___ (to work) at seven o’clock yesterday evening.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: Look, he ___ (to clean) his car! Now it’s shining.
explanation: We use ‘has’ with ‘he, she, it’. We see the result of an action in the Present - the car is shining. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: The lesson ___ (to begin) at 8 o’clock.
explanation: begin - began - begun. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I’m thirsty. I ___ (to buy) something to drink.
explanation: We use the Future Simple for decisions taken at the moment of speaking.

task: ___ was the party last night? - Oh, it was great!
explanation: We use ‘how’ when we want to know ‘in what way, to what extent’.

task: Sandra is my sister. ___ is very beautiful.
explanation: She = a subject pronoun, 3rd person, singular, female.

task: I can find ___ who can answer your question.
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences.

task: I wake up ___ 7 o’clock every morning.
explanation: At 7 o’clock, at 10.30, at midnight, at noon, at the moment, etc.

task: Mike is ___ (short) than Tom.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -(e)r to one-syllable words to make comparatives.

task: Mike ___ Sandra are my best friends.
explanation: We use ‘and’ to join two parts of the sentence (words, phrases, related statements).

task: Fred ___ a dentist.
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: Why ___ you late yesterday?
explanation: We use ‘were’ with we/you/they. ‘Are’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: Rachel ____ in Ottawa.
explanation: I/we/you/they — live. He/she/it — lives. ‘is living’ is the Present Continuous which is incorrect here. The speaker talks in general.

task: ___ you go to work yesterday?
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. ‘Did’ — the correct auxiliary verb in the Past Simple.

task: Mary ___ (to play) tennis while Mark ___ (to read) a book.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: I can’t find my wallet. I think I ___ (to lose) it.
explanation: We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’. We see the result of an action in the Present - I can’t find my wallet. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I ___ (to buy) two tickets to the theatre.
explanation: buy - bought - bought. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: Sarah’s birthday ___ (to fall) on Monday next month.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: ___ is your favourite movie? - ‘The Godfather’.
explanation: We use ‘what’ when we want to know information about things and actions in general. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices.

task: __ like ice cream, __ likes pancakes.
explanation: We should use a subject pronoun in this sentence.

task: There’s ___ in the dark.
explanation: ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things. ‘Something’ is used in positive sentences, ‘anything’ — in negative sentences.

task: Are you free ___ Sundays?
explanation: On: Sunday, Sundays, 10 May, Christmas Day, my birthday, etc.

task: My house is ___ (large) than yours.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -r to adjectives with -e ending to make comparatives.

task: It was sunny outside, ___ we decided to stay at home.
explanation: We use ‘but’ to connect two parts of the sentence. These parts have contrasting ideas.

task: We ___ a family.
explanation: We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: Your purse is nice. ___ it expensive?
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb. ‘Had’ cannot be used here.

task: Choose the correct word order
vars: She always gets up at 7 o’clock.
She gets always up at 7 o’clock.
She gets up at 7 o’clock always.
She gets up always at 7 o’clock.
explanation: Pronoun/name + adverbs of time + verb

task: Sarah ___ (to buy) two books three days ago.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple. ‘Buy’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘bought’.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: What were doing you at 8 o’clock yesterday evening?
Were you doing what at 8 o’clock yesterday evening?
You were doing what at 8 o’clock yesterday evening?
What were you doing at 8 o’clock yesterday evening?
explanation: The correct word order: question word + was/were + subject + verb with -ing + complement

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
explanation: We put ‘already, just, never’ after have/has and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: Jeremy has ___ (to drink) too much beer.
explanation: drink - drank - drunk. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: There are dark clouds in the sky. It ___ (to rain) soon.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ in predictions when we have evidence that something will happen in the nearest future.

task: There are two cars near our office. ___ is yours?
explanation: We use ‘which’ to get specific information. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices. ‘Who’ is used for a person.

task: This car is broken. __ needs to be repaired.
explanation: We should use a subject pronoun in this sentence.

task: Linda couldn’t find ___ who could help her open the window.
explanation: Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences.

task: Jill was born ___ 2002.
explanation: In: May, 1999, the 1990s, winter, the next century, the future, etc.

task: He’s much ___ (happy) than before.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We change -y to -i and add -er/-est.

task: Which will you choose: this red dress ___ the green one?
explanation: We use ‘or’ to connect two or more alternatives.

task: My favourite animal ___ a cat.
explanation: An animal = it. We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + was/were + pronoun/noun + complement

task: Mary ____ ____ alcohol.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t drink. He/she/it — doesn’t drink. ‘Does/doesn’t’ take ‘s’ from a verb.

task: She ___ (to study) chemistry when she was young. Now she’s 83.
explanation: She’s not young now, so the time period mentioned in the first part is over = the Past Simple. ‘Study’ is regular but we change the ending: -y = -ied.

task: Sam and Mary ___ (to do) their homework when I ___ (to come) home.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (were doing homework) when another one interrupted it (I came home). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: Is Carla at home? — I’m afraid she ___ (just/to go).
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: He’s ___ (to find) a good job.
explanation: find - found - found. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Paul ___ (to meet) his relatives this weekend. They have an arrangement.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: ___ will he come? - I don’t know. I thought he would come at 10:30.
explanation: We use ‘when’ to get information about time.

task: Please, don’t be angry with ___ . I did it accidentally.
explanation: This sentence requires an object pronoun. The correct object pronoun for ‘I’ is ‘me’.

task: There's hardly ___ here. There are few people at the art exhibition.
explanation: ‘Hardly’ means ‘almost not’, so it has a negative feeling. That’s why we need to use ‘anybody’.

task: I don’t like to wake up early ___ the morning.
explanation: We say ‘in the morning / in the mornings’, but ‘on Monday morning / on Monday mornings’.

task: Mary is ___ (intelligent) than Rachel.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We use ‘more’ if an adjective has two or more syllables.

task: Tom spoke quietly ___ the baby slept.
explanation: We use ‘because’ to connect the result and the reason in one sentence.

task: How old ___ you?
explanation: We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: When he ___ a pupil he ___ the best in his class. Now he’s 35.
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. 'Is/are' are used in the present. Now he’s 35, it means he’s an adult.

task: He ____ history at the university.
explanation: I/we/you/they — study. He/she/it — studies. ‘y’ - ‘ies’.

task: The bell ___ (to ring) suddenly.
explanation: Ring = rang

task: This time last week I ___ (to travel) across Australia.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action in the middle of happening at a stated time in the past.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: I haven’t read the book yet.
I haven’t yet read the book.
I yet haven’t read the book.
I haven’t read yet the book.
explanation: We put ‘yet’ in the end of a sentence.

task: She ___ (to give) me a book yesterday.
explanation: give - gave - given. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I think that all people ___ (to drive) electric cars in 2080.
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose the correct question.
vars: Who does wash the dishes in your family?
Who washes the dishes in your family?
Does who wash the dishes in your family?
Who the dishes washes in your family?
explanation: ‘Who’ is the subject in this question. We don’t use the auxiliary verb.

task: I was very angry but I told ___ to calm down.
explanation: This sentence requires a reflexive pronoun. The correct reflexive pronoun for ‘I’ is ‘myself’.

task: Is there ___ in the house to open the door for me?
explanation: We use ‘anybody’ in questions.

task: I’m going to the GYM ___ this evening.
explanation: We don’t use a preposition before ‘this morning/evening/etc.’, ‘last week/May/etc.’, ‘next week/May/etc.’, ‘every day/week/May/etc.’

task: The frost is much ___ (bad) at night.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. Bad - worse - the worst.

task: She was very beautiful ___ she was young.
explanation: ‘When’ means ‘at the time that’.

task: Choose the correct word order.
explanation: The correct word order in questions: auxiliary + subject + complement

task: ___ Sarah surprised to see her ex-boyfriend yesterday?
explanation: ‘Was’ is used with singular nouns or when we speak about one person. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb. ‘Is’ is used in the present. We speak about the past (yesterday) in this sentence.

task: She ____ work at 9 o’clock.
explanation: I/we/you/they — finish. He/she/it — finishes. When the verb ends in -ch, -ss, -sh, -x or -zz, we add -es.

task: Our friends ___ (to come) to see us last Sunday.
explanation: Last Sunday = the Past Simple. ‘Come’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘came’.

task: I ___ (to take) a shower when she ___ (to call) me.
explanation: We use the past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was taking a shower) when another one interrupted it (called). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Have ever you been to Rome?
Have you ever been to Rome?
Have you been ever to Rome?
Have you been to Rome ever?
explanation: We put ‘ever’ after the noun or the pronoun and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: Mike’s already ___ (to leave).
explanation: leave - left - left. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I can’t open the door. ___ (you/to help) me?
explanation: We use the Future Simple for requests, hopes, offers and promises. Here: a request.

task: Choose the correct question.
vars: Who Sandra saw in the park?
Who Sandra did see in the park?
Did who Sandra see in the park?
Who did Sandra see in the park?
explanation: ‘Who’ is the object in this question. We use the auxiliary verb.

task: ___ car is red, ___ is black. (you / I)
explanation: We should use a possessive adjective (you = your) in the first part of the sentence. In the second one we should use a possessive pronoun (I = mine).

task: ___ ___ (to want) to go outside.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb.

task: The train is leaving ___ ten minutes.
explanation: We use ‘in’ with these expressions: in 5 minutes/a few days/two weeks/two years, etc.

task: Canada is a bigger country ___ Italy.
explanation: If we want to compare things we use ‘than’.

task: Take a shower ___ you go to bed!
explanation: ‘Before’ suggests that the second action happens after the first one.

task: ___ you married?
explanation: We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: How ___ you now? You ___ sick two days ago.
explanation: The first question is in the present, so we use ‘are’. The second part is in the past (two days ago) so we use ‘were’.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Do you always sing in the shower?
Do you sing in the shower always?
Do you sing always in the shower?
Do always you sing in the shower?
explanation: do/does + pronoun/name + adverb of frequency + verb

task: He ___ (to put) the keys on the table.
explanation: Put = put

task: Jessy ___ (to walk) in the park at ten o’clock yesterday morning.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: I ___ (never/to ride) a horse.
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I ___ (to meet) him an hour ago.
explanation: meet - met - met. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: We need to hurry up! The train ___ (to leave) at 9.30.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: ___ car is it? - It’s mine.
explanation: We use ‘whose’ to know which person owns a thing.

task: I woke up and washed ___ .
explanation: Some verbs don’t normally take a reflexive pronoun after them. They are: wash, shave, dress, meet, rest, relax, get up, wake up, etc.

task: I can see ___ in the class. Everyone ___ gone.
explanation: ‘Nobody’ means ‘not anybody’.’Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb.

task: Sandra is waiting for you ___ the bus stop.
explanation: We use ‘at’ for the point, ‘in’ for an enclosed space, ‘on’ for a surface.

task: Mark is ___ (tall) boy in the team.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. We add ‘the’ and -(e)st to adjectives with one syllable.

task: I take a shower and change clothes ___ the workout. My clothes become wet during the workout.
explanation: ‘After’ suggests that the second action happens before the first one.

task: Thank you. That ___ very kind of you.
explanation: We use 'is' with ‘that’.

task: There ___ three beautiful horses in the field. I still remember them.
explanation: We use 'were' with plural nouns = three horses. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present. ‘I still remember them’ means that the speaker talks about the past.

task: My brother ____ driving big cars.
explanation: I/we/you/they — enjoy. He/she/it — enjoys. When the verb ends in a vowel + -y we just add -s.

task: Monica ___ (to take) off her coat and ___ (to sit) down.
explanation: Monica can’t take off her coat and sit down regularly, so the Present Simple is incorrect in this sentence. ‘Take’ and ‘sit’ are irregular = ‘took’ and ‘sat’.

task: Tom ___ (to stop) reading and ___ (to look) out of the window. Children ___ (to play) in the street.
vars: was stopping / was looking / were playing
explanation: For short actions (stopped and looked) we choose the Past Simple. For a longer action (were playing), to show that it was in progress before Tom looked out of the window and continued when he looked out of the window, we choose the Past Continuous.

task: Chris and Mary ___ (to be) married for 10 years.
explanation: ‘For 10 years’ means that they are still married, so the action that started 10 years ago continues up to now. ‘For, since’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: They’ve ___ (to sell) their house.
explanation: sell - sold - sold. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Nancy ___ (to play) tennis with Matthew tomorrow. They’ve arranged to meet at 9 o’clock.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: ___ did he leave the country? - He found a job abroad.
explanation: We use ‘why’ to know the reasons and get explanations.

task: Charlie, behave ___ !
explanation: ‘Behave yourself!’ is an idiom that means ‘be good!’.

task: Linda didn’t know ___ at the party.
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. We can’t use ‘nobody’ here because it would lead to a double negation which is not correct in English.

task: Bill has come here ___ the bus.
explanation: We use ‘on’ with these expressions: on a bus/train/plane, on the way.

task: It was ___ (good) film I’ve ever seen.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. Good - better - the best

task: Mike is older ___ Chris.
explanation: ‘Than’ is used to introduce the second part in a comparison.

task: It ___ nine o’clock. You ___ late.
explanation: We use 'is' with it and ‘are’ with you.

task: This singer ___ very popular in 1980s.
explanation: ‘Was’ is used with singular nouns or when we speak about one person. ‘Is’ - used for the present. We use 'were' with plural nouns. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: I ____ ____ much about football.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t know. He/she/it — doesn’t know.

task: Yesterday it ____ (to snow) all morning. It ____ (to stop) at 12 p.m.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. Finished action in the past and exact time in the past (at 12 p.m.) = the Past Simple.

task: He ___ (to talk) on his phone while he ___ (to drive) to work.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: ___ (you/to see) Kathy yesterday?
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple.

task: He ___ (to write) her a message five minutes ago.
explanation: write - wrote - written. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: Perhaps, it ___ (to rain) tomorrow.
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Do you know if has he a dog?
Do you know if he has a dog?
Do you know if he a dog has?
Do you know has if he a dog?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: John is only 17, but he lives by ___ .
explanation: ‘By himself’ = on his own.

task: Jerry is running all over the house. Is he looking for ___ ? — Yes, he can’t find his driving license.
explanation: We can use ‘somebody/something’ in questions when we expect a positive answer or when we make an offer or request.

task: Jill was very tired. She decided to go ___ home.
explanation: We say ‘go/come/walk home’, but ‘stay/work at home’.

task: Karen is ___ tall ___ I am.
explanation: We use ‘as + adjective + as’ to show that one thing has the same quality with another.

task: I sent him the invitation to the party, ___ he didn’t accept it.
explanation: We use ‘but’ to connect two parts of the sentence. These parts have contrasting ideas.

task: Here ___ your book.
explanation: Your book = it. We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: __ you know where the children are? - Oh my God, they ___ here a few minutes ago!
explanation: The first question is in the present, so we use the auxiliary ‘do’. The second part is in the past (a few minutes ago) so we use ‘were’. ‘Was’ is incorrect because we use it with singular nouns or when we speak about one person.

task: He usually ____ French but now he ____ ____ Italian.
explanation: general meaning = Present Simple / at the moment = Present Continuous

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Where he did go last night?
He did go last night where?
Where did he go last night?
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + did + pronoun/noun + complement

task: He ___ (to walk) down the street when he suddenly ___ (to hear) someone’s cry.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was walking) when another one interrupted it (heard a cry). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: He ___ (to be) at the office a few minutes ago. But he ___ (to go), I can’t find him.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple. ‘I can’t find him’ shows the result of an action in the Present, so we use the Present Perfect.

task: She's finally ___ (to choose) the red dress.
explanation: choose - choose - chosen. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Andrew ___ (to enter) the college next year. He’s made a decision.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ for actions we have already decided to do in the future.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Can you tell me what time it is?
Can you tell me what is time it?
Can you tell me is what time it?
Can you tell me what time it?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: After a hard day she was very pleased with ___ .
explanation: We should use a reflexive pronoun in this sentence. She = herself.

task: There ___ ___ wrong with the car.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb. ‘Something’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anything’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences.

task: They arrived ___ Spain ___ 13:30 and then got ___ the hotel.
explanation: We arrive in a country or town, get to the hotel. We use ‘at’ with: 7 o’clock, at 10.30, at midnight, at noon, at the moment, etc.

task: The ___ (high) you climb, the ___ (dangerous) it gets.
explanation: When one thing depends on the other, we can use ‘the’ with comparative adjectives.

task: I asked him a question ___ he came in.
explanation: ‘When’ means ‘at the time that’.

task: I ___ cold. I need to put on a sweater.
explanation: We use ‘am’ with I.

task: Jessy ___ at work three hours ago.
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: He ____ ____much time at the GYM.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t spend. He/she/it — doesn’t spend. ‘

task: He ____ (to listen) to the music yesterday.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. Regular verb + -ed = listen + -ed = listened.

task: We ___ (to have) dinner at six o’clock yesterday evening.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: Oh no, they ___ (to go). There’s nobody in.
explanation: We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’. We see the result of an action in the Present - there’s nobody in. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: He ___ (to break) the window yesterday.
explanation: break - broke - broken. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I'm hungry. I ___ (to find) a cafe where we can have a meal.
explanation: We use the Future Simple for decisions taken at the moment of speaking.

task: ___ old is your sister? - She’s 10.
explanation: We use ‘how’ when we want to know ‘in what way, to what extent’.

task: Our boss is from Canada. ___ is very smart.
explanation: He = a subject pronoun, 3rd person, singular, male.

task: ___ has taken my bag.
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things.

task: He came ___ midnight.
explanation: At 7 o’clock, at 10.30, at midnight, at noon, at the moment, etc.

task: This car is ___ (cheap) than that one.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -(e)r to one-syllable words to make comparatives.

task: There are knives ___ spoons on the table.
explanation: We use ‘and’ to join two parts of the sentence (words, phrases, related statements).

task: My mother ___ a teacher.
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: They ___ asleep when you called yesterday.
explanation: We use ‘were’ with we/you/they. ‘Are’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: Choose the correct word order
vars: Does often she write to you?
Does she often write to you?
Does she write often to you?
Does she write to you often?
explanation: do/does + pronoun/name + adverb of frequency + verb

task: I ___ visit my family last month.
explanation: Last month = the Past Simple. ‘Did’ — the correct auxiliary verb in the Past Simple.

task: Jack ___ (to read) a newspaper while Rachel ___ (to cook) dinner.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: Jessica ___ (to cook) a cheesecake. We’re eating it now and It’s very delicious!
explanation: We use ‘has’ with ‘he, she, it’. We see the result of an action in the Present - we’re eating a cheesecake now. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: A cat ___ (to catch) a mouse.
explanation: catch - caught - caught. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: The game ___ (to begin) at 6 o’clock this evening.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: ___ is your name? - Carol.
explanation: We use ‘what’ when we want to know information about things and actions in general. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices.

task: __ is a teacher, __ am a doctor.
explanation: We should use a subject pronoun in this sentence.

task: I can’t see ___ in the dark.
explanation: ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things. ‘Something’ is used in positive sentences, ‘anything’ — in negative sentences.

task: What are you going to do ___ your birthday?
explanation: On: Sunday, Sundays, 10 May, Christmas Day, my birthday, etc.

task: Steve was ___ (close) to Mary than someone else.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -r to adjectives with -e ending to make comparatives.

task: John likes vegetables, ___ he’s allergic to carrots.
explanation: We use ‘but’ to connect two parts of the sentence. These parts have contrasting ideas.

task: They ___ at school.
explanation: We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: What ___ the weather like a week ago?
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present.

task: We often ____ to the cinema.
explanation: I/we/you/they — go. He/she/it — goes. ‘Are going’ is the Present Continuous which is incorrect here. The speaker talks in general.

task: Tom ___ (to fly)from Rome to Paris last Monday.
explanation: Last Monday = the Past Simple. ‘Fly’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘flew’.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Where were you driving at 10 o’clock yesterday morning?
Were where you driving at 10 o’clock yesterday morning?
Where you were driving at 10 o’clock yesterday morning?
Where were driving you at 10 o’clock yesterday morning?
explanation: The correct word order: question word + was/were + subject + verb with -ing + complement

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: I never have heard this song before.
I have never heard this song before.
I have heard never this song before.
I have heard this song before never.
explanation: We put ‘already, just, never’ after have/has and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: I’ve ___ (to eat) a wonderful cheesecake this morning.
explanation: eat - ate - eaten. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: The lightning has hit the trunk of a tree. It ___ (to fall) soon.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ in predictions when we have evidence that something will happen in the nearest future.

task: ___ airline did you choose: Air China or IndiGo?
explanation: We use ‘which’ to get specific information. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices. ‘Who’ is used for a person.

task: The teacher asked ___ to learn the poem by heart.
explanation: This sentence requires an object pronoun. The correct object pronoun for ‘she’ is ‘her’.

task: I think there’s ___ in the dark! I saw a silhouette of a man!
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things.

task: This rock band was very popular ___ the 1980s.
explanation: In: May, 1999, the 1990s, winter, the next century, the future, etc.

task: Jill is ___ (lazy) than Vicky.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We change -y to -i and add -er/-est.

task: Barbara doesn’t like coffee ___ tea.
explanation: We use ‘or’ to connect two or more alternatives. If there’s a negative verb in the sentence, we use ‘or’ instead of ‘and’.

task: His car ___ black.
explanation: A car = it. We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Were you afraid of dogs when you were 10?
You were afraid of dogs when you were 10?
Afraid of dogs were you when you were 10?
Were afraid of dogs you when you were 10?
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + was/were + pronoun/noun + complement

task: He ____ $1500 for his apartments every month.
explanation: I/we/you/they — pay. He/she/it — pays. When the verb ends in a vowel + -y we just add -s.

task: I ___ (to stop) the car to check the map.
explanation: ‘Stop’ is regular, but we add the second ‘p’ + -ed = stopped.

task: It ___ (to rain) heavily when we ___ (to get) up.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was raining) when another one interrupted it (got up). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: She ___ (to finish) her lesson yet.
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should the Present Perfect Tense.

task: She’s ___ (to fly) to London this evening.
explanation: fly - flew - flown. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: He ___ (to fly) to Canberra tomorrow evening. He’s bought a one-way ticket.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: ___ are you going to fly to London? - Next week.
explanation: We use ‘when’ to get information about time.

task: Could you give this book to ___ ? (we)
explanation: This sentence requires an object pronoun. The correct object pronoun for ‘we’ is ‘us’.

task: Jack hardly ate ___ .
explanation: ‘Hardly’ means ‘almost not’, so it has a negative feeling. That’s why we need to use ‘anything’.

task: He wakes up late ___ Sunday mornings.
explanation: We say ‘in the morning / in the mornings’, but ‘on Sunday morning / on Sunday mornings’.

task: This book is ___ (interesting) than the previous one.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We use ‘more’ if an adjective has two or more syllables.

task: Tim was angry at me ___ I crashed his car.
explanation: We use ‘because’ to connect the result and the reason in one sentence.

task: Jessica and I ___ good friends.
explanation: Jessica + I = we. We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: You ___ very upset yesterday. What happened?
explanation: We use ‘were’ with we/you/they. ‘Are’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: I ____ home on foot now, but I usually ____ a taxi.
explanation: at the moment = Present Continuous / general meaning = Present Simple

task: He ___ (to pay) the bill.
explanation: Pay = paid

task: This time last month Daniel ___ (to work) as a secretary.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action in the middle of happening at a stated time in the past.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
explanation: We put ‘yet’ in the end of a sentence.

task: Jake’s ___ (to forget) to call his parents this morning.
explanation: forget - forgot - forgotten. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I think he ___ (not to come).
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose the correct question.
explanation: ‘Who’ is the subject in this question. We don’t use the auxiliary verb.

task: Tom accidentally cut ___ with the knife.
explanation: This sentence requires a reflexive pronoun. The correct reflexive pronoun for ‘he’ is ‘himself’.

task: Is there ___ in the box?
explanation: We use ‘anything’ in questions.

task: Jake’s leaving ___ next Tuesday.
explanation: We don’t use a preposition before ‘this morning/evening/etc.’, ‘last week/May/etc.’, ‘next week/May/etc.’, ‘every day/week/May/etc.’

task: The movie was ___ (good) than I expected.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. Good - better - the best.

task: ___ I entered the room, I saw Carla.
explanation: ‘When’ means ‘at the time that’.

task: Choose the correct word order.
explanation: The correct word order in questions: a question word + noun that describes a subject + auxiliary + subject

task: When they ___ young they played tennis very well. Now they’re too old to play it.
explanation: We use ‘were’ with we/you/they. ‘Are’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Chris goes never to the swimming pool.
Chris never goes to the swimming pool.
Chris goes to the swimming pool never.
Chris goes to the swimming never pool.
explanation: Pronoun/name + adverbs of time + verb

task: I ___ (to eat) the oatmeal porridge in the morning. Now it’s evening, I don’t want to eat it again.
explanation: The morning is finished, now it’s evening, so we use the Past Simple in the first part of the sentence. ‘Eat’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘ate’.

task: Lisa ___ (to drink) coffee when Robert ___ (to see) her.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was drinking). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Has ever Mary been to Canada?
Has Mary been to Canada ever?
Has Mary been ever to Canada?
Has Mary ever been to Canada?
explanation: We put ‘ever’ after the noun or the pronoun and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: He ___ (to hear) a loud sound.
explanation: hear - heard - heard. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I swear I ___ (never/to do) this again.
explanation: We use the Future Simple for requests, hopes, offers and promises. Here: a promise.

task: Choose the correct question.
vars: Who he talked to so long yesterday?
Who he did talk to so long yesterday?
Who did he talk to so long yesterday?
Did he talk to who so long yesterday?
explanation: ‘Who’ is the object in this question. We use the auxiliary verb.

task: This is ___ house, that house is ___ . (she / we)
explanation: We should use a possessive adjective (she = her) in the first part of the sentence. In the second one we should use a possessive pronoun (we = ours).

task: ___ ___ (to like) the new car.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb.

task: Let’s meet ___ a few days!
explanation: We use ‘in’ with these expressions: in 5 minutes/a few days/two weeks/two years, etc.

task: My brother is three years older ___ me.
explanation: If we want to compare things we use ‘than’.

task: I have breakfast ___ I go to work.
explanation: ‘Before’ suggests that the second action happens after the first one.

task: ___ these your books?
explanation: Books = they. We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: Where ___ you yesterday?
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present. We speak about the past in this sentence (yesterday).

task: He ____ to do his best.
explanation: I/we/you/they — try. He/she/it — tries. ‘y’ - ‘ies’.

task: She ___ (to try) the dress on.
explanation: ‘Try’ is regular but we change the ending: -y = -ied.

task: She ___ (to swim) in the pool at five o’clock yesterday evening.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: They ___ (never/to see) the leopard.
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense. We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’.

task: Oh my God, I’ve ___ (to lose) my keys!
explanation: lose - lost - lost. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: The bus ___ (to arrive) at 12 p.m. tomorrow.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: ___ house has been burnt? - Tom’s.
explanation: We use ‘whose’ to know which person owns a thing.

task: I got ___ up early.
explanation: Some verbs don’t normally take a reflexive pronoun after them. They are: wash, shave, dress, meet, rest, relax, get up, wake up, etc.

task: I can see ___ in the box. It’s empty.
explanation: ‘Nothing’ means ‘not anything’.

task: Father is working ___ the garden.
explanation: We use ‘at’ for the point, ‘in’ for an enclosed space, ‘on’ for a surface.

task: This is ___ (big) circus I’ve ever seen.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. We add ‘the’ and -(e)st to adjectives with one syllable.

task: We can’t play loudly ___ parents have gone to bed.
explanation: ‘After’ suggests that the second action happens before the first one.

task: He ___ interested in art but I ___ fond of football.
explanation: We use 'is' with he and ‘am’ with I.

task: There ___ a girl with a balloon, as far as I remember.
explanation: Correct explanation: ‘Was’ is used with singular nouns or when we speak about one person. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present. ‘As far as I remember’ means that the speaker talks about the past.

task: Mike ____ in a shop.
explanation: I/we/you/they — work. He/she/it — works. ‘is worked’ is an incorrect form.

task: Jake ___ (to take) a shower and ___ (to drink) a cup of coffee.
explanation: Take = took, drink = drank

task: Linda ___ (to stop) talking to her friend and ___ (to turn) over. A big van ___ (to move) slowly towards them.
vars: was stopping / was turning / was moving
explanation: For short actions (stopped and turned over) we choose the Past Simple. For a longer action (was moving), to show that it was in progress before Linda stopped talking and continued when she turned over, we choose the Past Continuous.

task: I ___ (to know) her since 2004.
explanation: ‘Since 2004’ means that the action started in 2004 and continues up to now. ‘For, since’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: He ___ (to put) his umbrella under the table yesterday.
explanation: put - put - put. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: Lisa ___ (to come) to see us tomorrow. We’ve decided to meet at 20.00.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: ___ are you late? - I’m sorry, I missed the bus.
explanation: We use ‘why’ to know the reasons and get explanations.

task: Hello, friends! Enjoy ___ !
explanation: ‘Enjoy yourselves’ is an idiom that means ‘have a good time’.

task: She hasn’t read ___ during her holidays.
explanation: ‘Something’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anything’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. We can’t use ‘nothing’ here because it would lead to a double negation which is not correct in English.

task: Rachel is ___ her way home.
explanation: We use ‘on’ with these expressions: on a bus/train/plane, on the way.

task: He's made ___ (bad) decision in his entire life.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. Bad - worse - the worst.

task: He came earlier ___ usual.
explanation: ‘Than’ is used to introduce the second part in a comparison.

task: Here ___ your crayons.
explanation: Crayons = they. We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: She ___ in Paris now, but two days ago she ___ in London.
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is’ - used for the present. We speak about the past in this sentence (two days ago).

task: He often ____ the documentaries.
explanation: I/we/you/they — watch. He/she/it — watches. When the verb ends in -ch, -ss, -sh, -x or -zz, we add -es.

task: The excursion was very long. It ____ (to start) at 10.30 and ___ (to end) at 17.40.
explanation: Finished action in the past and exact time in the past (at 10.30 and 17.40 p.m.) = the Past Simple.

task: Tom ___ (to sleep) while the cat ___ (to eat).
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: Where ___ (you/to go) last night?
explanation: Last night = the Past Simple.

task: She ___ (to speak) too loud.
explanation: speak - spoke - spoken. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I’m sure, they ___ (to win).
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Can you tell me whether does she live in London?
Can you tell me whether she does live in London?
Can you tell me whether she lives in London?
Can you tell me whether lives she in London?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: This little girl has cooked dinner by ___ .
explanation: ‘By herself’ = on her own.

task: Would you like ___ to drink?
explanation: We can use ‘somebody/something’ in questions when we expect a positive answer or when we make an offer or request.

task: Sandra is staying ___ home today.
explanation: We say ‘go/come/walk home’, but ‘stay/work at home’.

task: Mary swims ___ a fish.
explanation: We use ‘like’ when two things/qualities are similar. ‘As’ means ‘in the role of’.

task: Miriam ___ Lora are very beautiful.
explanation: We use ‘and’ to join two parts of the sentence (words, phrases, related statements).

task: It ___ rainy today, but it ___ cold.
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: Today the weather ___ awesome, but yesterday it ___ very bad.
explanation: The first part is about the present (today), so we use ‘is’. The second one is about the past (yesterday), so we use ‘was’.

task: They ____ ____ football very often.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t play. He/she/it — doesn’t play.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: What time did you get up yesterday?
What time you did get up yesterday?
Did what time you get up yesterday?
What time did get up you yesterday?
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + did + pronoun/noun + complement

task: He ___ (to play) the guitar when the phone ___ (to ring).
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was playing) when another one interrupted it (the phone rang). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: He ___ (to buy) a new dress for his wife yesterday. She ___ (to see) it yet.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I ___ (to feel) sorry for her that day.
explanation: feel - felt - felt. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: Emily ___ (to leave) the country next month. She’s already decided to do it.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ for actions we have already decided to do in the future.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Do you know how much does it cost?
Do you know how much it costs?
Do you know does how much it cost?
Do you know how much it does cost?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: Jake was proud of ___ . Jake won the game yesterday.
explanation: We should use a reflexive pronoun in this sentence. He = himself.

task: There ___ ___ wrong with the laptop.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb. ‘Something’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anything’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences.

task: John was very tired when he arrived ___ home.
explanation: We say ‘get/arrive home’.

task: The ___ (good) you learn, the ___ (smart) you get.
explanation: When one thing depends on the other, we can use ‘the’ with comparative adjectives.

task: Which do you prefer? Roses ___ peonies?
explanation: We use ‘or’ to connect two or more alternatives.

task: I ___ hungry. Let’s go to the cafe.
explanation: We use ‘am’ with I.

task: Tom ___ 20 last year. Now he’s 21.
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: It ____ a lot of money to build a stadium.
explanation: I/we/you/they — cost (is not used with these pronouns). He/she/it — costs. ‘is costing’ is the Present Continuous which is incorrect here. The speaker talks in general.

task: She ____ (to enjoy) the party last night.
explanation: Last night = the Past Simple. Regular verb + -ed = enjoy + -ed = enjoyed.

task: He ___ (to watch) television at eleven o’clock yesterday morning.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: I ___ (to finish) the letter. Now I can send it.
explanation: We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’. We see the result of an action in the Present - now I can send the letter. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: She ___ (to bring) a stray kitten to the office.
explanation: bring - brought - brought. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I like this bag. I ___ (to buy) it.
explanation: We use the Future Simple for decisions taken at the moment of speaking.

task: ___ far is it from here to the park? - About six kilometres.
explanation: We use ‘how’ when we want to know ‘in what way, to what extent’.

task: __ are my best friend.
explanation: You = a subject pronoun, 2nd person, singular.

task: ___ has broken the window.
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things.

task: I’m very busy ___ the moment.
explanation: At 7 o’clock, at 10.30, at midnight, at noon, at the moment, etc.

task: This way is ___ (long) than the previous one.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -(e)r to one-syllable words to make comparatives.

task: The weather was warm ___ sunny.
explanation: We use ‘and’ to join two parts of the sentence (words, phrases, related statements).

task: Carla’s daughter ___ a singer.
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: We ___ very hungry and decided to have dinner.
explanation: We use ‘were’ with we/you/they. ‘Are’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: You ____ ____ hard.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t work. He/she/it — doesn’t work.

task: We ___ plan to go the party yesterday.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. ‘Did’ — the correct auxiliary verb in the Past Simple.

task: Mike ___ (to work) while Carol ___ (to clean) the flat.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: Oh, you ___ (to paint) a dog house. It looks great now!
explanation: We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’. We see the result of an action in the Present - it looks great now. That’s why we use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: He ___ (to come) home at 20 o’clock.
explanation: come - came - come. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: The train from Berlin ___ (to arrive) at 10:40.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: ___ time is it? - It’s 10:30.
explanation: We use ‘what’ when we want to know information about things and actions in general. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices.

task: __ are tennis players, __ are footballers.
explanation: We should use a subject pronoun in this sentence.

task: He hasn’t come yet. ___ has happened.
explanation: ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things. ‘Something’ is used in positive sentences, ‘anything’ — in negative sentences.

task: Goodbye, John! See you ___ Wednesday!
explanation: On: Sunday, Sundays, 10 May, Christmas Day, my birthday, etc.

task: This place is much ___ (safe) than the previous one.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We add -r to adjectives with -e ending to make comparatives.

task: He’s got the license, ___ he hasn’t bought a car yet.
explanation: We use ‘but’ to connect two parts of the sentence. These parts have contrasting ideas.

task: You ___ a good driver.
explanation: We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: ___ Tom and Mary at the theatre last Sunday?
explanation: We use 'were' with plural nouns or when we speak about two or more people (Tom and Mary). ‘Are’ is used in the present. ‘Was’ is used with singular nouns or when we speak about one person. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: It seems she ____ her hands a hundred times a day.
explanation: I/we/you/they — wash. He/she/it — washes. When the verb ends in -ch, -ss, -sh, -x or -zz, we add -es.

task: Fred always goes to work by car but yesterday he ___ (to go) to work by bus.
explanation: Yesterday = the Past Simple. ‘Go’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘went’.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Were why you sleeping at 11 o’clock yesterday morning?
Why you were sleeping at 11 o’clock yesterday morning?
Why were sleeping you at 11 o’clock yesterday morning?
Why were you sleeping at 11 o’clock yesterday morning?
explanation: The correct word order: question word + was/were + subject + verb with -ing + complement

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: They have already discussed the problem.
They already have discussed the problem.
They have discussed already the problem.
They have discussed the problem already.
explanation: We put ‘already, just, never’ after have/has and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: It’s already autumn so leaves have ___ (to fall) off trees.
explanation: fall - fell - fallen. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I crashed the company car. My boss ___ (not to be) happy when he knows about it.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ in predictions when we have evidence that something will happen in the nearest future.

task: ___ is bigger: the Statue of Liberty or the Eiffel Tower?
explanation: We use ‘which’ to get specific information. ‘What’ is used when there is a big variety of things to choose. ‘Which’ is used when there is a small number of possible choices. ‘Who’ is used for a person.

task: ___ wants Jill to apologise.
explanation: We should use a subject pronoun in this sentence.

task: Everyone has gone. I can’t see ___ inside.
explanation: ‘Somebody’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anybody’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. ‘Something’ and ‘anything’ are used with things.

task: I’ll have a vacation ___ summer.
explanation: In: May, 1999, the 1990s, winter, the next century, the future, etc.

task: That task was much ___ (easy).
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We change -y to -i and add -er/-est.

task: I don’t like snowboarding ___ skiing.
explanation: We use ‘or’ to connect two or more alternatives. If there’s a negative verb in the sentence, we use ‘or’ instead of ‘and’.

task: It ___ cloudy today.
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: They were tired after the journey?
Were they tired after the journey?
They tired were after the journey?
Tired after the journey were they?
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + was/were + pronoun/noun + complement

task: This little car ____ ____ much petrol.
explanation: I/we/you/they — don’t spend. He/she/it — doesn’t spend.

task: She ___ (to plan) to go for a walk an hour ago.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple. ’Plan’ is regular, but we add the second ‘n’ + -ed = planned.

task: Betty ___ (to drive) home when Jeremy ___ (to call).
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was driving home) when another one interrupted it (Jeremy called). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: Mike ___ (already/to see) this movie.
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: They have already ___ (to go) to work.
explanation: go - went - gone. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Steven ___ (to visit) the dentist this Tuesday. They have an arrangement.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: ___ did he join the group? - Last week.
explanation: We use ‘when’ to get information about time.

task: He received a message from ___ a minute ago. (she)
explanation: This sentence requires an object pronoun. The correct object pronoun for ‘she’ is ‘her’.

task: It was very noisy in the room. She could hardly hear ___ .
explanation: ‘Hardly’ means ‘almost not’, so it has a negative feeling. That’s why we need to use ‘anything’.

task: He usually goes to work ___ Monday mornings.
explanation: We say ‘in the morning / in the mornings’, but ‘on Monday morning / on Monday mornings’.

task: This sofa is ___ (comfortable) than another one.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. We use ‘more’ if an adjective has two or more syllables.

task: I’m going to bed ___ I’ll have to wake up early tomorrow.
explanation: We use ‘because’ to connect the result and the reason in one sentence.

task: Those candies ___ delicious.
explanation: Candies = they. We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: There ___ a pink purse on the shelf. I didn’t know who left it.
explanation: ‘Was’ is used with singular nouns or when we speak about one person. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present.

task: She ____ chess every Monday.
explanation: I/we/you/they — play. He/she/it — plays. When the verb ends in a vowel + -y we just add -s.

task: I ___ (to see) him three days ago.
explanation: See = saw

task: This time last year James ___ (to live) in Spain.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action in the middle of happening at a stated time in the past.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
explanation: We put ‘yet’ in the end of a sentence.

task: He ___ (to know) everything about her behaviour.
explanation: know - knew - known. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I’m afraid she ___ (to be) on time for the dinner.
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose the correct question.
explanation: ‘Who’ is the subject in this question. We don’t use the auxiliary verb.

task: They blamed ___ for losing the game.
explanation: This sentence requires a reflexive pronoun. The correct reflexive pronoun for ‘they’ is ‘themselves’.

task: Is there ___ to eat in the fridge?
explanation: We use ‘anything’ in questions.

task: Carl goes to the swimming pool ___ every week.
explanation: We don’t use a preposition before ‘this morning/evening/etc.’, ‘last week/May/etc.’, ‘next week/May/etc.’, ‘every day/week/May/etc.’

task: Mary eats ___ (little) chocolate than she used to.
explanation: This sentence requires a comparative adjective, not a superlative one. Little - less - the least

task: ___ the store opens, I’ll go there every day.
explanation: ‘When’ means ‘at the time that’.

task: Choose the correct word order.
explanation: The correct word order in questions: a question word + auxiliary + subject

task: She ___ very happy to meet Mark. She hadn’t seen him since 2010.
explanation: We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. ‘Is’ - used for the present. ‘Did’ is not used without a verb.

task: He ____ right now, but he usually ____ free time watching movies.
explanation: at the moment = Present Continuous / general meaning = Present Simple

task: He ___ (to build) a dog house in the garden a month ago.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple. ‘Build’ is irregular. Its correct form in the past is ‘built’.

task: Nancy ___ (to read) when her cat ___ (to break) the vase.
explanation: We use the past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was reading) when another one interrupted it (broke). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Have you ever read this book?
Have you read this book ever?
Have ever you read this book?
Ever have you read this book?
explanation: We put ‘ever’ after the noun or the pronoun and before the verb in the Past Participle form.

task: She's finally ___ (to make) a decision.
explanation: make - made - made. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: I ___ (to buy) these shoes, ok?
explanation: We use the Future Simple for requests, hopes, offers and promises. Here: an offer.

task: Choose the correct question.
explanation: ‘Who’ is the object in this question. We use the auxiliary verb.

task: ___ book is green, ___ is grey.
explanation: We should use a possessive adjective (we = our) in the first part of the sentence. In the second one we should use a possessive pronoun (they = theirs).

task: ___ ___ (to have) a right to vote in this country.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb.

task: We’re moving to Spain ___ two months.
explanation: We use ‘in’ with these expressions: in 5 minutes/a few days/two weeks/two years, etc.

task: As for me, Messi is a better player ___ Ronaldo.
explanation: If we want to compare things we use ‘than’.

task: He reads ___ he goes to bed.
explanation: ‘Before’ suggests that the second action happens after the first one.

task: ___ it cold today?
explanation: We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: ___ your exam difficult yesterday? Yes, it ___ .
explanation: Both parts are about the past. So we can’t use ‘is/are’. We use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it.

task: They never ____ talk shows.
explanation: I/we/you/they — watch. He/she/it — watches. ‘are watching’ is the Present Continuous which is incorrect here. The speaker talks in general.

task: Rachel ___ (to copy) Tom’s text and ___ (to send) it to me.
explanation: ‘Copy’ is regular but we change the ending: -y = -ied. ‘Send’ is irregular = sent.

task: She ___ (to listen) to music at four o’clock yesterday evening.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for an action that was in progress at a stated time in the past.

task: We ___ (never/to be) to New Delhi.
explanation: ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet, never’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense. We use ‘have’ with ‘we, they, I, you’.

task: I ___ (to read) that newspaper yesterday.
explanation: read - read - read. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: The film ___ (to start) at 11:00 AM according to the programme.
explanation: We use the Present Simple to talk about events in the future that will certainly happen, for schedules, timetables and programmes.

task: __ umbrella is this? - Linda’s.
explanation: We use ‘whose’ to know which person owns a thing.

task: Tom shaved ___ quickly and ate breakfast.
explanation: Some verbs don’t normally take a reflexive pronoun after them. They are: wash, shave, dress, meet, rest, relax, get up, wake up, etc.

task: Jack is very lazy. He does ___ to make his life better.
explanation: ‘Nothing’ means ‘not anything’.

task: He lives ___ the 5th floor.
explanation: We use ‘at’ for the point, ‘in’ for an enclosed space, ‘on’ for a surface.

task: It was ___ (sad) moment in her entire life.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. We add ‘the’ and -(e)st to adjectives with one syllable.

task: We’ll deliver the order ___ you pay the bill. We can’t deliver it if we don’t get the money first.
explanation: ‘After’ suggests that the second action happens before the first one.

task: I ___ 20 and Jenny ___ 23.
explanation: We use ‘am’ with I and ‘is’ with she.

task: There ___ ten cars near our house. They were parked about a week ago.
explanation: We use 'were' with plural nouns = ten cars. ‘Is/are’ - used for the present. ‘A week ago’ means that the speaker talks about the past.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: What does he usually do in the morning?
What does he do usually in the morning?
What does he do in the morning usually?
What usually does he do in the morning?
explanation: question word + do/does + pronoun/name + adverb of frequency + verb

task: She ___ (to write) a message and ___ (to go) away.
explanation: Write = wrote, go = went

task: Joseph ___ (to hear) the noise and ___ (to go) out to the street. The crowd of young protesters ___ (to move) down the street.
vars: was hearing / was going / was moving
explanation: For short actions (heard and went out) we choose the Past Simple. For a longer action (was moving), to show that it was in progress before Joseph heard the noise and continued when he went out, we choose the Past Continuous.

task: He ___ (to be) hungry for three hours.
explanation: ‘For three hours’ means that the action started 3 hours ago and continues up to now. ‘For, since’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: She's already ___ (to take) a medicine.
explanation: take - took - taken. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Mark ___ (to fly) to Madrid tomorrow morning. He’s already bought the tickets.
explanation: We use the Present Continuous with future meaning for fixed arrangements in the near future.

task: __ are you so sad? - I’ve lost my job.
explanation: We use ‘why’ to know the reasons and get explanations.

task: Hi, Peter! Make ___ at home!
explanation: ‘Make yourself’ is an idiom that means ‘feel comfortable’.

task: I have never seen ___ like that.
explanation: ‘Something’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anything’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences. We can’t use ‘nothing’ here because it would lead to a double negation which is not correct in English.

task: Who is this girl ___ the picture?
explanation: We say 'in a photograph / in a picture’.

task: This is ___ (little) expensive dress in this store.
explanation: This sentence requires a superlative adjective, not a comparative one. Little - less - the least

task: My project is better ___ hers.
explanation: ‘Than’ is used to introduce the second part in a comparison.

task: Hey, there ___ Peter outside!
explanation: Peter = he. We use ‘is’ with she, he, it.

task: He ___ very angry at me yesterday. Today he ___ speak to me.
explanation: The first sentence: we use ‘was’ with I/he/she/it. The second one is about the present (today), so we use ‘doesn’t’. We don’t say ‘he is speak to me’.

task: She always ____ when she watches dramas.
explanation: I/we/you/they — cry. He/she/it — cries. ‘y’ - ‘ies’.

task: They ____ (to go) to the park last evening and ____ (to return) very late.
explanation: Last evening = the Past Simple. ‘Go’ is irregular = ‘went’. ‘Return’ is regular = ‘returned’.

task: He ___ (to smile) while he ___ (to look) at her.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous for two or more simultaneous actions. ‘While’ shows that actions are simultaneous.

task: She ___ (to finish) her work two hours ago.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple.

task: He was very tired but ___ (to keep) on moving.
explanation: keep - kept - kept. We use the second form in the Past Simple Tense.

task: I believe he ___ (to pass) the exam.
explanation: We use the Future Simple to make a prediction based on what we think, believe or imagine; with expressions ‘be sure, be afraid’, adverbs ‘perhaps, certainly’, etc.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Can you tell me if can Sam swim?
Can you tell me if Sam can swim?
Can you tell me if Sam swim can?
Can you tell me can if Sam swim?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: These tiny stray puppies live by ___ in the streets.
explanation: ‘By themselves’ = on their own.

task: You haven’t eaten since morning. Would you like ___ to eat?
explanation: We can use ‘somebody/something’ in questions when we expect a positive answer or when we make an offer or request.

task: Did you walk ___ home?
explanation: We say ‘go/come/walk home’, but ‘stay/work at home’.

task: He works ___ a manager in the shop.
explanation: We use ‘like’ when two things/qualities are similar. ‘As’ means ‘in the role of’.

task: You can have a glass of apple juice ___ a cup of tea.
explanation: We use ‘or’ to connect two or more alternatives. If there’s a negative verb in the sentence, we use ‘or’ instead of ‘and’.

task: Her cards ___ on the table.
explanation: Cards = they. We use ‘are’ with we, they, you.

task: Last Monday he ___ late for work. Today he ___ also late.
explanation: The first part is about the past (last Monday), so we use ‘was’. The second one is about the present (today), so we use ‘is’.

task: Choose the correct word order
vars: Sarah plays sometimes tennis with her friends.
Sarah plays tennis sometimes with her friends.
Sarah plays tennis with her friends sometimes.
Sarah sometimes plays tennis with her friends.
explanation: Pronoun/name + adverbs of time + verb

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
explanation: The correct word order: a question word + did + pronoun/noun + complement

task: He ___ (to go) to the museum when he ___ (to receive) the message.
explanation: We use the Past Continuous to show that one action was in progress (was going to the museum) when another one interrupted it (received the message). The second part of the sentence describes a short action, so we use the Past Simple.

task: It ___ (to start) raining an hour ago. It ___ (to finish) raining yet.
explanation: Ago = the Past Simple. ‘Just, already, ever, recently, yet’ show that we should use the Present Perfect Tense.

task: She has ___ (to swim) five kilometres.
explanation: swim - swam - swum. We use the Past Participle (the third form) in the Present Perfect Tense.

task: Sandra ___ (to start) learning French next year. She’s decided to do it.
explanation: We use ‘be going to’ for actions we have already decided to do in the future.

task: Choose a sentence with the correct word order.
vars: Do you know where he spent last weekend?
Do you know where did he spend last weekend?
Do you know where he did spend last weekend?
Do you know where spent he last weekend?
explanation: After ‘can you tell me’, ’do you know’, etc., we use the same word order as in statement sentences.

task: It’s unbelievable how Linda ___ could organise the celebration.
explanation: To emphasise that Linda could organise the celebration without anyone’s help, we should use a reflexive pronoun in this sentence. She = herself.

task: There ___ ___ wrong with the cell phone.
explanation: ‘Anybody/somebody, anything/something, everybody/everything’ are 3rd person pronouns and followed by a singular verb. ‘Something’ is used with people, mainly in positive sentences. ‘Anything’ is also used with people but in questions and negative sentences.

task: What time do you usually go ___ bed? — ___ 22:30, but I like reading ___ bed and then fall asleep.
explanation: We go to bed and read in bed. We use ‘at’ with: 7 o’clock, at 10.30, at midnight, at noon, at the moment, etc.

task: The ___ (old) you get, the ___ (wise) you become.
explanation: When one thing depends on the other, we can use ‘the’ with comparative adjectives.

task: It was dark, ___ he could see the robber.
explanation: We use ‘but’ to connect two parts of the sentence. These parts have contrasting ideas.
